examples.en: Someone manipulated the photo.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 투표 결과를 조작한 사람을 잡았대요.
examples.en: The news said they caught the person who rigged the voting results.
You must not falsify data.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 서류를 조작해서 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That company forged documents, and it became a problem.
There was someone who tried to fabricate evidence.
Let's check whether the video was doctored.

explain: '조작하다'는 사진, 서류, 결과처럼 사실이 아닌 것을 일부러 만들 때 써서 나쁜 일에 많이 나와요. 기계나 장치를 다루는 뜻으로도 써서 '기계를 조작하다'처럼 말해요. '조작이에요'처럼 명사 '조작'으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: 조작하다 is used when someone deliberately fabricates something untrue, such as a photo, a document, or a result, so it often appears in bad-news contexts. It is also used for operating a machine or device, as in '기계를 조작하다'. The noun 조작 is common too, as in '조작이에요'.

examples.en: Height is measured accurately at the hospital.
This morning's temperature was measured below zero.
The measured number is different every day.
The sound level will be measured by a machine.

examples.ko: 시험을 보면 실력이 측정되고 순위도 나와요.
examples.en: When you take the test, your skill is measured and a ranking comes out.

examples.ko: 미세먼지 농도가 높게 측정돼서 마스크를 썼어요.
examples.en: The fine dust level was measured as high, so I wore a mask.

explain: '측정하다'의 피동이라서 재는 사람보다 '재어진 결과'가 중심일 때 써요. 숫자나 기계가 나오는 글, 뉴스, 설명에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서 사람이 직접 잴 때는 '재다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This is the passive of 측정하다, used when the measured result matters more than who measured it. It appears in news, reports and explanations with numbers or instruments. In daily talk, when a person measures something, 재다 is more common.

examples.en: This fruit is imported from the Philippines.
Many new cars were imported last year.
Imported meat is cheaper.

examples.ko: 내일 새 제품이 한국으로 수입될 거예요.
examples.en: The new product will be imported into Korea tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이 커피는 브라질에서 수입돼서 맛이 좋아요.
examples.en: This coffee is imported from Brazil, so it tastes good.

examples.ko: 외국에서 수입된 물건에는 표시가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Goods imported from abroad have a label on them.

explain: 반대말은 '수출되다'예요. 물건이 어느 나라에서 들어오는지 말할 때 '~에서 수입되다'로 써요. 마트에서는 '수입산'이라는 말도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The opposite is 수출되다. You say '~에서 수입되다' to say which country goods come from. At the supermarket you will often see the label 수입산, meaning imported.

en: be wary of; be on guard against; watch out for

examples.en: You should be wary of strangers.
Our puppy is wary of guests.

examples.ko: 그는 처음 만난 사람을 경계하는 편이에요.
examples.en: He tends to be on guard with people he first meets.
The news told people to beware of scam calls.
The cat approached slowly, wary of me.
Don't be so guarded, let's talk comfortably.

explain: '조심하다'는 일반적인 주의이고, '경계하다'는 나쁜 일이 생길까 봐 의심하며 지켜보는 느낌이 강해요. 사람, 동물, 위험한 것을 목적어로 자주 써요. '경계를 풀다'처럼 명사 '경계'와 같이 쓰는 말도 많아요.
explain_en: 조심하다 is general carefulness, while 경계하다 feels more suspicious, as if watching for something bad to happen. Its objects are usually people, animals or dangers. The noun 경계 also appears in set phrases like '경계를 풀다'.

examples.en: Korea has a well-developed subway system.
Children develop in body and mind while playing.
I want to work in a country with advanced technology.
If you exercise, your muscles will develop more.
As the internet developed, shopping became easy.
The tourism industry is well developed in this area.

explain: '발달하다'가 '스스로 발전하다'라면 '발달되다'는 '발달된 상태'를 강조해요. '발달돼 있다', '발달된 기술'처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요. 사람이나 도시가 '좋아지고 커지는' 쪽의 변화에 써요.
explain_en: 발달하다 is closer to 'grows by itself', while 발달되다 stresses the developed state. It often shows up as '발달돼 있다' or '발달된 기술'. It describes people, cities or fields growing and getting better.

examples.en: Reading develops your ability to think.
The teacher developed the child's language skills.
To develop your muscles, you must exercise every day.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 농업을 발달시킨 덕분에 부자가 됐어요.
examples.en: That country became rich thanks to developing its farming.

examples.ko: 악기 연주는 손을 발달시키는 좋은 방법이에요.
examples.en: Playing an instrument is a good way to develop your hands.
I'm looking for a game that will develop the senses.

explain: '발달하다'는 저절로 자라는 것이고, '발달시키다'는 누군가가 힘이나 기술을 키울 때 써요. 능력, 근육, 산업처럼 키울 수 있는 것을 목적어로 해요. 비슷한 말 '키우다'는 아이, 식물, 실력 모두에 쓰는 더 쉬운 말이에요.
explain_en: 발달하다 happens by itself, while 발달시키다 is used when someone builds up an ability or skill. Its objects are things you can grow, such as abilities, muscles or industries. The simpler 키우다 works for children, plants and skills alike.

examples.en: The luggage is kept in the lobby.

examples.ko: 오래된 사진이 상자 안에 보관돼 있었어요.
examples.en: The old photos were stored in a box.
I drank the milk that was kept in the fridge.
The documents will be kept for five years.

examples.ko: 이 약은 시원한 곳에 보관돼야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine has to be stored in a cool place.

examples.ko: 영수증이 잘 보관되면 나중에 교환할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the receipt is kept safe, you can exchange it later.

explain: '보관하다'의 피동이라서 물건이 어디에 있는지 말할 때 써요. 호텔 안내문, 약 설명서처럼 '~에 보관하세요' 글에서 자주 만나요. 일상에서 사람이 직접 '두다', '넣어 두다'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: This is the passive of 보관하다 and tells where something is kept. You see the active form in hotel notices and medicine labels like '~에 보관하세요'. In daily speech people more often say 두다 or 넣어 두다.

examples.en: The main character takes revenge on the bad guy in the movie.
He said he would take revenge for his friend.
Will I feel at ease after taking revenge?
He prepared for a long time in order to get revenge.
In the drama, the person who took revenge ends up regretting it.
How about forgiving instead of taking revenge?

explain: '복수하다'는 드라마, 영화, 소설에 자주 나오는 말이고 일상에서는 장난으로 쓰기도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '갚아 주다'나 '되갚다'가 비슷한 상황에 더 가볍게 쓰여요. 같은 소리의 '복수(여럿)'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: 복수하다 is common in dramas, movies and novels, and people sometimes use it jokingly. In casual talk, 갚아 주다 or 되갚다 fits similar situations in a lighter way. Don't confuse it with another word 복수 that means 'plural'.

examples.en: People these days consume a lot of goods.

examples.ko: 이 차는 기름을 적게 소비해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This car is popular because it uses little fuel.

examples.ko: 한 달에 얼마나 소비하는지 적어 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote down how much I spend a month.
Let's try to cut down on things that use energy.
I used up too much time.
I try not to spend wastefully.

explain: '소비하다'는 돈, 물건, 에너지, 시간을 써서 없애는 것을 두루 말해요. '쓰다'가 일상어라면 '소비하다'는 경제나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요. '소비자', '소비 생활'처럼 명사와 합친 말이 많아요.
explain_en: 소비하다 covers using up money, goods, energy or time. 쓰다 is the everyday word, while 소비하다 appears more in economics and news. It also forms many compounds such as 소비자 (consumer).

examples.en: The two people's opinions match.
The name doesn't match the document.
Our hobbies matched, so we became close quickly.
I like people whose words and actions match.
If our times match, let's go together.
The police said the fingerprints matched.

explain: '일치하다'는 '~와/과 일치하다'처럼 비교하는 두 대상이 둘 다 필요해요. 주어가 '둘'이면 '의견이 일치하다'처럼 쓸 수도 있어요. 반대말은 '다르다', '일치하지 않다'예요.
explain_en: 일치하다 needs two things being compared, as in '~와/과 일치하다'. If the subject itself is plural, as in 의견이 일치하다, no second noun is needed. The opposite is 다르다 or 일치하지 않다.

examples.en: The elevator suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 비밀번호를 세 번 틀리면 계정이 정지돼요.
examples.en: If you get the password wrong three times, the account is suspended.
I captured the frozen screen.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 오전에는 공장 기계가 정지될 거예요.
examples.en: The factory machines will be stopped in the morning because of the construction.
When the car stopped, people got off.
My driver's license was suspended, so I can't drive.

explain: '멈추다'와 달리 '정지되다'는 기계, 계정, 면허처럼 '누가 멈추게 한' 것에 주로 써요. 사람이 걷다가 멈출 때는 '멈추다', '서다'를 써요. 기계·서비스의 '일시 정지'는 '일시 정지돼요'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike 멈추다, 정지되다 mostly describes machines, accounts or licenses that were stopped by something. For a person stopping while walking, use 멈추다 or 서다. For machines and services, '일시 정지되다' means 'temporarily suspended'.

examples.en: The driver brought the bus to a stop.

examples.ko: 문제가 생기면 기계를 바로 정지시켜야 해요.
examples.en: If a problem occurs, you must stop the machine right away.

examples.ko: 회사는 규칙을 어긴 계정을 정지시키려고 해요.
examples.en: The company plans to suspend accounts that broke the rules.
You can pause the video and ask a question.

examples.ko: 비상 버튼을 누르면 열차를 정지시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can stop the train by pressing the emergency button.
Please explain the reason for shutting down the factory.

explain: '정지되다'는 멈춰진 결과이고, '정지시키다'는 사람이 멈추게 하는 동작이에요. 기계, 차, 계정처럼 누군가 통제하는 대상에 써요. 일상에서 영상을 멈출 때는 '멈추다'나 '일시 정지하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 정지되다 describes something that has been stopped, while 정지시키다 is the action of making it stop. It fits machines, vehicles or accounts that someone controls. For pausing a video in daily talk, people say 멈추다 or 일시 정지하다.

examples.en: The manager made the new employee attend the meeting.
The school has students attend the event.
Please don't force the child to attend.
The CEO wants to have all the team members attend.
Many companies have employees attend training.
I asked whether we could have guests attend.

explain: '참석하다'는 본인이 가는 것이고, '참석시키다'는 다른 사람을 가게 하는 거예요. 회사와 학교처럼 위에서 정하는 상황에서 쓰고, 친구 사이에서는 잘 안 써요. 가볍게는 '오게 하다', '보내다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 참석하다 is going yourself, while 참석시키다 is getting someone else to go. It fits company or school settings where someone in charge decides, and rarely appears between friends. Casually, people say 오게 하다 or 보내다.

examples.en: The school accepted ten people.

examples.ko: 선생님이 학생들을 모두 합격시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The teacher wants to get all the students to pass.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 두 명만 합격시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The company will only admit two people this year.

examples.ko: 이 학원은 많은 학생을 합격시키는 것으로 유명해요.
examples.en: This academy is famous for getting many students to pass.

examples.ko: 시험 위원들이 그 학생을 합격시키기로 했어요.
examples.en: The exam committee decided to pass that student.
They gave good scores but still didn't pass them.

explain: '합격하다'는 시험을 보는 사람이 붙는 것이고, '합격시키다'는 학교, 회사, 선생님이 붙게 해 주는 쪽이에요. 시험 결과를 말할 때는 '합격하다'가 훨씬 많이 쓰여요. 반대말은 '불합격시키다', '떨어뜨리다'예요.
explain_en: 합격하다 is from the point of view of the test taker who passes, while 합격시키다 is from the side of the school, company or teacher who lets them pass. In everyday talk about results, 합격하다 is far more common. The opposite is 불합격시키다 or 떨어뜨리다.

examples.ko: 이 건물에서는 음식을 먹는 것을 허용하지 않아요.
examples.en: Eating food is not allowed in this building.
The school allows the use of cell phones.
My parents allowed me to come home late.
The company decided to allow working from home.
Let's do it within what the rules allow.
I'm looking for a home that permits pets.

explain: '허용하다'는 규칙이나 기관이 '해도 된다'고 정할 때 써서 글과 안내문에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '허락하다'나 '되다'를 써요. 반대말은 '금지하다'예요.
explain_en: 허용하다 is used when a rule or institution says something is allowed, and it is common in written notices. In everyday talk, 허락하다 or the plain 되다 is more usual. The opposite is 금지하다.

examples.en: The content of the call is recorded automatically.
I was surprised that my voice was recorded.

examples.ko: 수업이 녹음돼서 다시 들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The class is recorded, so you can listen again.
I sent the recorded song to my friend.
I didn't know the meeting was being recorded.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 소리가 녹음될 때 빨간 불이 켜져요.
examples.en: This app shows a red light when sound is being recorded.

explain: '녹음하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '녹음되다'는 소리가 저절로 저장된 상태를 말해요. 전화, 수업, 회의처럼 기록이 남는 상황에 자주 나와요. 영상은 '녹화되다', 화면은 '캡처되다'로 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: 녹음하다 is something a person does, while 녹음되다 describes sound that has been saved. It often appears with calls, classes and meetings. For video you say 녹화되다, and for a screen you say 캡처되다.

examples.en: Please refer to the manual.
It's easy to understand if you refer to the picture.

examples.ko: 저는 다른 글을 참조해서 보고서를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote the report by referring to other writing.
For details, please see the table below.
It's good to consult several sources.

examples.ko: 그 자료를 참조했는데도 답을 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: I looked at that material but still couldn't find the answer.

explain: '참조하다'는 '확인하세요' 대신 안내문, 설명서, 보고서에서 자주 써요. '보세요'보다 글로 쓴 말투이고, 일상 대화에서는 '참고하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 이메일의 '참조(CC)'도 같은 한자어예요.
explain_en: 참조하다 appears in notices, manuals and reports to say 'see this'. It sounds more written than 보세요, and in daily talk 참고하다 is more common. The email field 참조 (CC) uses the same word.

examples.en: I sometimes think fondly of my school days.
I looked at old photos with my friends and reminisced.
Grandmother smiled as she looked back on her youth.
That song makes me recall last summer.

examples.ko: 우리는 같이 여행한 날을 추억하곤 해요.
examples.en: We often look back on the day we traveled together.
I'm happy because I have a lot to look back on.

explain: '추억하다'는 좋았던 옛날을 따뜻하게 떠올릴 때 써요. 나쁜 기억에는 보통 쓰지 않아요. 일상 대화에서는 '그때가 생각나요', '추억이 있어요'처럼 명사 '추억'을 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 추억하다 is for warmly recalling good times in the past, and is not usually used for bad memories. In daily talk people more often use the noun, as in '추억이 있어요' or '그때가 생각나요'.

examples.en: Two cars collided at the intersection.
Our opinions often clash.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 서로 충돌해서 만날 수 없어요.
examples.en: Our appointment times conflict, so we can't meet.
There are many accidents where birds hit windows.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 크게 충돌한 뒤 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: After the two people had a big clash, they don't talk.

examples.ko: 일정이 충돌하지 않게 미리 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check ahead so the schedules don't conflict.

explain: '충돌하다'는 물건끼리 부딪힐 때도, 사람의 생각이나 일정이 안 맞을 때도 써요. 가볍게 몸이 닿을 때는 '부딪히다'를 쓰고 '충돌하다'는 크고 세게 부딪히는 느낌이에요. 일정이나 의견이 맞지 않을 때는 '겹치다', '맞지 않다'도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 충돌하다 is used both when objects crash and when opinions or schedules conflict. For light contact, 부딪히다 is used, while 충돌하다 feels bigger and harder. For schedules and opinions, 겹치다 or 맞지 않다 are also common.

examples.en: He withdrew the lawsuit.
To withdraw the report, you must go to the police station.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 화해해서 고소를 취하하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two made up and decided to drop the complaint.

examples.ko: 신청서를 취하한 사람은 다시 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person who withdrew an application can submit it again.
The lawyer advised withdrawing the request.
The company withdrew its patent application.

explain: 주로 소송, 고소, 신청 같은 법이나 서류와 관련된 일에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 약속이나 주문을 없앨 때는 '취소하다'를 써요. '취하'와 '취소'는 비슷하지만 '취하'는 내가 낸 것을 거두는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: This is a formal word used for legal or paperwork matters such as lawsuits, complaints and applications. For canceling plans or orders in daily life, use 취소하다. 취하하다 leans toward taking back something you yourself filed.

examples.en: I put a face mask on in the evening.
I'll go buy a carton of milk.
I stick a straw into the juice carton and drink.
My skin is dry, so I do face masks often.
There are two packs of tofu in the fridge.

examples.ko: 즉석밥 팩 하나로 간단하게 한 끼를 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had a simple meal with one pack of instant rice.

explain: 한국에서 '팩'은 얼굴에 붙이는 '마스크 팩'을 가장 많이 가리켜요. 우유나 주스 같은 종이 용기는 '우유팩'처럼 불러요. 세는 말로도 써서 '두 팩'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea, 팩 most often means a face mask pack. Paper cartons for milk or juice are called things like 우유팩. It also works as a counter, as in '두 팩'.

examples.en: A camera monitors the building entrance.
The police are watching a suspicious person.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 휴대폰을 감시하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like Mom is monitoring my phone.
The teacher watched the students during the exam.

examples.ko: 밤새 불이 안 나게 감시해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to watch all night so no fire breaks out.
I joined a group that monitors the environment.

explain: '감시하다'는 나쁜 일이 생기지 않게 지켜보거나 의심하며 보는 거라 조금 차가운 느낌이에요. 그냥 보는 '보다'와 달라요. 명사 '감시'는 '감시 카메라'처럼 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: 감시하다 means watching to prevent or catch something bad, so it feels cold and suspicious. It differs from plain 보다. The noun 감시 is common, as in 감시 카메라 (surveillance camera).

examples.en: A lawyer went to the trial on my behalf.
Someone representing the manager came to the meeting.
I submitted the documents on behalf of my father.
I can't act on behalf of the boss.

examples.ko: 대신 일해 줄 분이 팀장님을 대리했어요.
examples.en: The person who worked in their place acted for the team leader.
Please first tell me whom you represent.

explain: '대신하다'는 일반적인 말이고, '대리하다'는 회사나 법에서 다른 사람 자리에서 공식적으로 일할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '대신 해 주다'가 더 자연스러워요. 직급 '대리'와 소리가 같아서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: 대신하다 is the general word, while 대리하다 is for officially acting in someone's place at a company or in law. In daily talk, 대신 해 주다 sounds more natural. It sounds the same as the job rank 대리, which is easy to mix up.

examples.en: I borrowed three books from the library.

examples.ko: 은행이 저에게 집 살 돈을 대출했어요.
examples.en: The bank lent me money to buy a house.

examples.ko: 신분증이 있으면 책을 대출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can borrow books if you have an ID.

examples.ko: 은행은 돈을 대출해 줄 때 서류를 확인해요.
examples.en: Banks check documents when they lend money.
The borrowing period is two weeks.

examples.ko: 대출한 책은 다음 주까지 돌려줘야 해요.
examples.en: You must return the borrowed book by next week.

explain: '대출하다'는 도서관에서는 책을 빌릴 때도 빌려줄 때도 써요. 은행에서는 돈을 빌려주는 쪽이 '대출하다', 빌리는 쪽이 '대출받다'예요. 책은 '대출', '반납'으로 말하고, 은행 돈은 '대출을 받다', '갚다'로 말해요. 일상에서 '책을 빌리다'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: At a library, 대출하다 is used both for borrowing and lending a book. At a bank, the lender 대출하다 and the borrower says 대출받다. Library books go with 대출 and 반납, bank money with 대출을 받다 and 갚다. In everyday speech, '책을 빌리다' is the most natural way to say you borrowed a book.

examples.en: I put a cover on my new phone.
I washed the bed cover and hung it out.
I bought the book because its cover is pretty.
This song is a cover by a famous singer.
The chair cover got dirty.

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 자전거 커버를 덮어 둘게요.
examples.en: Since it's raining, I'll put a cover over the bike.

explain: '커버'는 휴대폰, 침대, 책처럼 위를 덮는 물건에 널리 써요. 책의 겉은 '표지', 휴대폰은 '케이스'라고도 해요. 노래를 다른 가수가 다시 부르는 '커버곡'에도 써요.
explain_en: 커버 is used widely for things that go over something, such as a phone, a bed or a book. A book's outside is also called 표지, and a phone cover is also called 케이스. It also appears in 커버곡, a song re-sung by another singer.

examples.en: Language is learned by repeating it.
This AI was trained on a lot of data.
A habit learned by a child lasts a long time.
It takes time for good habits to be learned.
Movements learned by the body come out naturally.

examples.ko: 이 내용은 이미 학습돼서 문제를 풀 수 있어요.
examples.en: This content has already been learned, so I can solve the problem.

explain: '학습되다'는 배우는 사람이 아니라 '배워진 결과'를 보는 말이에요. 인공지능이 데이터로 배우는 상황에서 특히 자주 써요. 사람이 직접 배울 때는 '배우다', '공부하다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 학습되다 looks at the result of being learned rather than the learner. It is especially common for AI learning from data. When a person learns directly, 배우다 or 공부하다 sounds much more natural.

examples.en: The researcher trains the computer.
The teacher makes the kids learn in a fun way.
We trained the AI with lots of photos.
If you force a child to study, they come to hate it.

examples.ko: 모델을 학습시키는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to train a model.

examples.ko: 음성 인식 모델을 학습시킬 데이터를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for data to train a speech recognition model.

explain: '학습시키다'는 컴퓨터나 인공지능을 훈련하는 말로 많이 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 '억지로 공부하게 하는' 느낌이 있어요. 아이나 학생에게는 '가르치다'가 더 따뜻하고 자연스러워요. 동물을 연습시킬 때는 '훈련시키다'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: 학습시키다 is common for training computers or AI, and when used for people it can feel like forcing them to study. For children or students, 가르치다 sounds warmer and more natural. For training animals, 훈련시키다 is common.

en: date; be in a romantic relationship

examples.en: I dated in college.
The two dated for three years and got married.
These days I'm busy and have no time to date.
My friend is in a relationship and looks happy.

examples.ko: 연애하면 좋은 점도 있고 힘든 점도 있어요.
examples.en: Dating has good points and hard points.
I heard a couple who dated for a long time broke up.

explain: '연애하다'는 서로 좋아하는 사이로 만나는 것을 말해요. '사귀다'는 '누구와 사귀어요'처럼 상대를 말할 때 편하고, '연애하다'는 연애하는 일 자체를 말할 때 자주 써요. '연애를 하다'처럼 '연애'와 '하다'를 나눠 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: 연애하다 means being in a romantic relationship. 사귀다 is handy when you name the partner, as in '누구와 사귀어요', while 연애하다 talks about the activity of dating itself. You can also split it as '연애를 하다'.

examples.en: The company is rolling out a new ad campaign.
The teacher developed the story in an interesting way.

examples.ko: 시민들이 환경 보호 운동을 전개하고 있어요.
examples.en: Citizens are carrying out an environmental protection campaign.
Order matters when you develop an argument.

examples.ko: 작가가 사건을 빠르게 전개해서 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: The writer moves the events along quickly, so it isn't boring.
Please tell me how to develop a piece of writing.

explain: '전개하다'는 이야기, 주장, 운동처럼 시작해서 점점 이어 가는 일에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '하다', '벌이다'가 비슷하게 쓰이고, 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 나와요. 명사 '전개'는 '이야기 전개가 빠르다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 전개하다 is used for stories, arguments or campaigns that start and then keep developing. In daily talk, 하다 or 벌이다 can fill a similar role, and 전개하다 appears more in writing and presentations. The noun 전개 is used like '이야기 전개가 빠르다'.

examples.ko: 저는 올해 안에 영어를 마스터하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to master English within this year.
You need practice to master that skill.
My friend mastered the guitar.

examples.ko: 한글을 마스터하는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took one month to master Hangul.

examples.ko: 게임 기술을 마스터한 뒤에 대회에 나갔어요.
examples.en: After mastering the game skills, I entered the contest.

examples.ko: 한 번에 다 마스터할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't master everything at once.

explain: '마스터하다'는 영어 master를 그대로 쓴 말이고, 일상 대화에서 '완전히 익히다'라는 가벼운 느낌으로 많이 써요. '익히다', '통달하다'는 더 단단하게 들려요. 보통 언어, 기술, 게임처럼 연습으로 늘리는 것에 써요.
explain_en: 마스터하다 borrows English 'master' and in daily talk has a light feel of 'fully getting the hang of it'. 익히다 and 통달하다 sound firmer. It is used for languages, skills and games that you improve through practice.

examples.en: Three people survived the accident.
It is hard for animals to survive without water.
I learned how to survive on a deserted island.

examples.ko: 그들은 추위 속에서 일주일 동안 생존할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: They were able to survive for a week in the cold.
For a small shop to survive, it needs customers.
What if dinosaurs still survived?

explain: '살아남다'는 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰고, '생존하다'는 뉴스와 글에서 자주 나와요. 사고, 재난, 자연처럼 어려운 상황 속에서 목숨이 이어질 때 써요. 가게나 회사가 '버티다'는 의미로도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: 살아남다 is more common in everyday talk, while 생존하다 appears in news and writing. It is used when life continues through difficult situations such as accidents, disasters or nature. It can also be used figuratively for a shop or company holding on.

examples.en: Our house is next to the school.
Which countries neighbor Korea?
I live in a neighborhood next to the market.
The two cities are adjacent, so they are close.

examples.ko: 두 학교가 이웃했을 때는 같이 행사를 했어요.
examples.en: When the two schools were next to each other, they held events together.
If an apartment is next to a park, the air is good.

explain: '이웃하다'는 '~와/과 이웃하다'나 '이웃한 ~'처럼 두 곳이 가깝게 붙어 있을 때 써요. 사람이 옆집에 산다고 말할 때는 '이웃에 살다'나 '옆집에 살다'가 더 자연스러워요. 'ㅎ' 때문에 [이우타다]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: 이웃하다 is used in forms like '~와/과 이웃하다' or '이웃한 ~' when two places lie close together. For a person living next door, 이웃에 살다 or 옆집에 살다 sounds more natural. Because of ㅎ, it is pronounced [이우타다].

examples.en: At Christmas the streets are decorated with lights.
The room was prettily decorated with flowers.
Paintings are displayed on the wall.
I saw that the cake was decorated with strawberries.
The party place will be decorated with balloons.

examples.ko: 예쁘게 장식되어 있는 카페라서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: The cafe was prettily decorated, so I took lots of photos.

explain: '장식하다'는 하는 사람이 있고, '장식되다'는 꾸며진 결과를 말해요. '~으로 장식되다'는 어떤 재료로 꾸몄는지 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '꾸미다', '꾸며져 있다'도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 장식하다 has a person doing it, while 장식되다 describes the decorated result. '~으로 장식되다' tells what the decoration is made of. In daily talk 꾸미다 and 꾸며져 있다 are also common.

examples.en: The phone was charged all night.
The battery charges up to 80 percent.
My transit card wasn't topped up, so I couldn't ride.
Please don't play games while it's charging.
When points are added, a text message comes.
Unplug it after it has charged enough.

explain: '충전하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고 '충전되다'는 에너지나 돈이 채워지는 상태를 말해요. 휴대폰 배터리, 교통카드, 포인트에 자주 써요. '쉬면서 에너지를 충전하다'처럼 사람에게 비유로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: 충전하다 is what a person does, while 충전되다 describes energy or money being filled in. It is common for phone batteries, transit cards and points. People also use 충전하다 figuratively, as in recharging energy by resting.

examples.en: If you practice every day, your skills improve.
My grades improved a lot since last year.
I feel my stamina improving when I exercise.
To improve your skills, you have to keep at it.
The service improved, so customers increased.
We will improve quality even more going forward.

explain: '향상하다'는 실력, 성적, 품질처럼 '좋은 쪽으로 올라가는' 변화에 써요. 나빠지는 변화에는 쓰지 않아요. 같은 뜻으로 '향상되다'도 많이 써서 '실력이 향상됐어요'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 향상하다 describes upward change in skills, grades or quality, and is never used for getting worse. 향상되다 is also very common, as in '실력이 향상됐어요'.

examples.en: Stars can be observed well in the night sky.
A strange change was observed in the experiment.

examples.ko: 이 새는 겨울에 주로 관찰되곤 해요.
examples.en: This bird is mainly seen in winter.

examples.ko: 작은 곤충의 움직임이 현미경으로 관찰되니까 신기해요.
examples.en: It's amazing that you can see the tiny insect's movement through the microscope.
If there are noticeable symptoms, go to the hospital.
No snow was observed this month.

explain: '관찰하다'는 사람이 자세히 보는 일이고, '관찰되다'는 '눈에 띄게 보인다'는 결과를 말해요. 과학, 뉴스, 보고서에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '보이다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 관찰하다 is a person watching carefully, while 관찰되다 states that something is seen or noticed. It is common in science, news and reports. In everyday talk, 보이다 is used more often.

examples.en: The company compensated the customer for the loss.
The insurance company covers the repair costs.
I'll make up for the plate I broke.

examples.ko: 늦게 와서 미안하니까 밥으로 보상하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm sorry I came late, so I want to make it up with a meal.

examples.ko: 사고 피해를 보상하는 방법을 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into how to compensate for the accident damage.
We have to reward the employees who worked hard.

explain: '보상하다'는 손해나 노력에 대해 돈이나 선물로 갚을 때 써요. '보답하다'는 고마움을 마음이나 행동으로 갚는 느낌이 더 커요. 일상에서는 '갚다', '보답하다'도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 보상하다 is used for paying back a loss or effort with money or gifts. 보답하다 leans toward repaying kindness with feeling or action. In daily talk, 갚다 and 보답하다 are also common.

examples.en: I wish love were everlasting.
Nothing in the world is eternal.
I hope our friendship lasts forever.
That song is eternal in my heart.
Happiness is not forever, but it is precious.
I want to be friends forever.

explain: '영원하다'는 끝이 없다는 느낌으로 노래, 영화, 편지 속 말에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '평생', '언제까지나'가 더 자주 들려요. 부사는 '영원히'예요: '영원히 잊지 않을게요'.
explain_en: 영원하다 has a feeling of no end and often appears in songs, movies and letters. In daily talk, 평생 or 언제까지나 are heard more often. The adverb is 영원히, as in '영원히 잊지 않을게요'.

en: get divorced; be divorced from; be separated by divorce

examples.en: My parents divorced when I was little.
I heard that couple decided to divorce.
After the divorce, she started new work.
I asked why they want to divorce.
My friend's parents got divorced and live separately.
I worried about how to live if I divorced.

explain: '이혼하다'는 '~와/과 이혼하다'로 쓰고 결혼한 사이에서만 말해요. 사귀는 사이에서 헤어지는 것은 '헤어지다'예요. 'ㅎ' 때문에 [이호나다]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: 이혼하다 is used as '~와/과 이혼하다' and only for married couples. For a couple that is dating, use 헤어지다. Because of ㅎ, it is pronounced [이호나다].

examples.en: If you break the law, you are punished.
That person was punished according to the law.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어긴 사람은 처벌될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person who breaks the rules can be punished.
I heard that the employee who lied was penalized.
Please don't do it, because it's punishable.

examples.ko: 잘못이 없는 사람이 처벌돼서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: A person who is not at fault must not be punished.

explain: '처벌하다'는 벌을 주는 쪽이고, '처벌되다'는 벌을 받는 쪽에서 말해요. 법, 학교 규칙처럼 공식적인 곳에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서 벌을 받을 때는 '벌받다', '혼나다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요.
explain_en: 처벌하다 is from the side giving the punishment, and 처벌되다 is from the side receiving it. It is used in formal settings such as law and school rules. In daily life, 벌받다 and 혼나다 are lighter words.

examples.en: The school announced the vacation schedule.
I posted a notice at the shop that we're closed tomorrow.
I'll announce important things in the group chat.

examples.ko: 변경된 시간을 공지하지 않아서 혼란이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because the changed time wasn't announced, confusion arose.

examples.ko: 회사가 이메일로 새 규칙을 공지하는 중이에요.
examples.en: The company is announcing the new rule by email.
As announced, class starts at 7.

explain: '공지하다'는 학교, 회사, 가게가 여러 사람에게 정해진 내용을 알릴 때 써요. 친구에게 개인적으로 알릴 때는 '알려 주다'를 써요. 명사 '공지'는 앱이나 홈페이지의 '공지사항'에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 공지하다 is used when a school, company or shop informs many people of a fixed matter. For telling a friend personally, use 알려 주다. The noun 공지 appears often as 공지사항 (notices) in apps and websites.

examples.ko: 피부가 물질에 접촉하면 가려울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If skin touches the substance, it can get itchy.

examples.ko: 환자와 접촉한 사람은 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: People who had contact with the patient must get tested.
I tried making contact with that company.
After touching animals, I wash my hands.

examples.ko: 외국인과 접촉하는 일이 많아서 영어가 필요해요.
examples.en: I meet foreigners a lot at work, so I need English.
Two wires touched and sparks flew.

explain: '접촉하다'는 몸이나 물건이 닿는 것뿐 아니라 사람이나 회사와 연락을 시작하는 것에도 써요. 가볍게 손을 대는 것은 '만지다'가 일상에서 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '접촉자', '접촉 사고'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 접촉하다 covers physical contact and also starting contact with a person or company. For lightly touching with the hand, 만지다 is more natural in daily talk. In news it appears as nouns such as 접촉자 (a contact) and 접촉 사고 (minor collision).

en: be approved; be consented; be permitted

examples.ko: 이곳에서는 사진 찍는 것이 허락되지 않아요.
examples.en: Taking photos is not permitted here.
My vacation was finally approved.
Going out is allowed until ten at night.
Only permitted people can enter.
With your parents' consent, it will be allowed.
I was really happy that my admission was approved.

explain: '허락하다'는 허락해 주는 사람이 중심이고, '허락되다'는 허락을 받은 결과를 말해요. '허용되다'가 규칙이 정해서 되는 것이라면 '허락되다'는 어떤 사람이 되게 해 준 느낌이에요. 일상에서는 '허락을 받다', '돼요'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 허락하다 centers on the person granting permission, while 허락되다 states the result of being permitted. 허용되다 feels like a rule allows it, whereas 허락되다 feels like a person let it happen. In daily talk, '허락을 받다' and plain 돼요 are more common.

examples.en: Please check whether it can be paid by card.
The ordered item is paid for automatically.

examples.ko: 실수로 같은 물건이 두 번 결제됐어요.
examples.en: The same item was charged twice by mistake.
A text arrives once it is paid, so please check.

examples.ko: 아직 결제되지 않아서 상품을 보낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been paid yet, so we can't send the goods.

examples.ko: 결제된 금액은 다음 달에 카드값에서 빠져요.
examples.en: The amount that was paid comes out of the card bill next month.

explain: '결제하다'는 사람이 돈을 내는 일이고, '결제되다'는 결제가 처리된 상태를 말해요. 앱, 인터넷 쇼핑, 카드 문자에서 자주 나와요. 가게에서 직접 낼 때는 '계산하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 결제하다 is a person paying, while 결제되다 states that the payment has been processed. It shows up in apps, online shopping and card text messages. At a shop counter, 계산하다 sounds more natural.
